evaluator: Final holdout A — PR-016, Prof. Warren Sack lens
evidence: The About page provides the required central comparison surface. It plainly states the recursive method: “observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue.”

That central surface compares Harry J. Epstein Company, FairRentNYC, WOWList, and Sunday Dinner/196 through consistent headings for relationships, interface and use, and learning and continuity without claiming the projects are equivalent.

At least three public-safe projects visibly support reconstruction of the full method. HJE connects customer and operational relationships to a maintained storefront, incremental releases, analytics-informed learning, reusable patterns, clearer workflows, and team continuity.

FairRentNYC connects collaborators, lived experience, public sources, policy questions, and government actors to campaign interfaces and collective public use, then to minutes, source maps, decision records, action trackers, and recoverable context.

WOWList connects organizers’ existing community vocabulary to a modeled keyword-community system, a public interface and publishing workflow used by real organizers, distribution learning, and reusable low-cost operating patterns.

Sunday Dinner/196 supplies bounded historical work: hospitality and trust relationships became invitations, onboarding, facilitation, access handoffs, recurring collective participation, and repeatable continuity practices while private histories remained excluded.

CallNYC further demonstrates the sequence through open-data interpretation, information architecture, an independent prototype, public engagement and reporting, iteration, public documentation, and explicit archival limitations.

Authorship and causality are bounded throughout: WOWList is “co-built”; FairRentNYC outcomes remain collective; CallNYC disclaims official City status; HJE uses contribution language; and coalition work explicitly rejects sole causation of policy outcomes.
Historical technologies are presented as the stack used for WOWList, not as proof of current proficiency. CallNYC is clearly marked archived, unofficial, and unsuitable for current guidance.

The source-backed-memory lab is explicitly early research/method/consulting practice—not production SaaS, a chatbot, or a replacement for judgment. Its synthetic example is labeled as such, avoiding invention claims.
The public course-completion certificate is precisely bounded as professional development, not instructor affiliation, endorsement, or production-product proof.
The reviewed links lead readers to project pages, public project surfaces, a public repository, or archived reporting and are described with appropriate scope boundaries.
safety_findings: No visible use of private UCSC narrative evaluations, private correspondence, or unapproved testimonials was found.

Private coalition notes, legal-review materials, stakeholder information, guest records, correspondence, analytics, customer data, and unapproved images are expressly kept outside the public surfaces.
The public course-completion artifact complies with the stated exception and is appropriately bounded.
